vi.drop_indices_note: Indices the pipeline never uses. The NEON VI zip ships five (ARVI, EVI, NDVI, PRI, SAVI); only SAVI, NDVI and EVI are read (instructions5.md 2A index priority). ARVI and PRI are deleted after download, with their _error.tif and .aux.xml companions, to avoid carrying dead weight across ~70 tiles.

511000_3532000.reason: Only 4.09% of the tile was flown - it sits on the northern edge of the AOP flight box. CHM is the binding product (nodata over 95.91% against 74.96% RGB and 66.79% SAVI), so stage 3 classified just 38,684 of 1,000,000 pixels. It was the ONLY Q4 train tile, so the entire Q4 training representation was a 4.1 ha sliver, and its leave-one-tile-out fold in run 3 was a 4 ha fold counted as a full tile.

520000_3532000.reason: Only 24.37% flown, and separately only 55.4% of the tile lies inside the PlanetScope footprint - roughly 14 ha of usable overlap between the two constraints. It was the only Q2 test tile.

tiles_retired.note: RETIRED FROM THE ACTIVE TILE SET, NOT DELETED. Both tiles are real, correctly processed ground - they are simply too small to carry the role they were given. Their labelling survives on disk in stage2_labeling/ (511000_3532000: 25 training polygons, 92 reviewed shrub candidates; 520000_3532000: 57 training polygons, 67 reviewed) and MUST NOT be deleted: it is valid hand-labelled data over flown ground and may be readmitted as supplementary training samples if a later run pools labels across tiles rather than treating each tile as a CV fold. What made them unusable is the ROLE, not the data - a 4 ha tile cannot stand as a quintile representative or a CV fold.
tiles_retired.selection_criteria_added: Neither tile would have been chosen under the criteria now in instructions5.md section 2A, because two of the four did not exist when the tile set was expanded from 5 to 10: (1) flight coverage ~100%, tested on CHM; (2) wholly inside the PlanetScope footprint. Measured over all 70 flown tiles, 60 pass the first, 63 the second, 54 both. The whole northern row at northing 3532000 - all ten tiles - is 4-24% flown.

decisions.rgb_nodata_undeclared: ACCEPTED - NEON RGB carries no nodata value; check 15 is informational, not a defect
decisions.chm_max_valid_m: CHM values above 15 m are man-made structures (towers) and are masked pipeline-wide
decisions.H_GRASS_MAX_measured: Set to 0.7 m from measurement, not assumption (instructions5.md section 3 safeguard 2). NEON CHM is pre-thresholded: minimum non-zero value is exactly 0.700 m on all five tiles, with nothing between 0 and 0.7. The previous 0.3 m was inert - any value in (0, 0.7] yields an identical shrub band. Consequence: woody vegetation below 0.7 m is structurally invisible to CHM and is recorded as 0, indistinguishable from bare ground.

stage1_7_generate_segments_RETIRED.retired: 2026-08-18. The script moved to unused/ - nothing consumed its output. See unused/README.md and results/stage3_results.md section 1.2. This key is KEPT rather than deleted because it records the parameters the existing segment_features_*.npz files were built with, which is their only provenance. No script reads it.

stage1_3_planet_grid.grid_source_year_note: The grid is year-invariant for a site, so it is derived from a year that exists on disk. SRER 2022 is pending generation and gates Step 5 only; Steps 3 and 4 need the geometry, not the phenology, and 2021 defines the same geometry. Switch to 2022 once it exists and confirm the checks still pass.
stage1_3_planet_grid.verification_variable_note: LSP layer exported as a GeoTIFF on the measured grid and loaded under the cell outlines in QGIS. EVIamp is chosen because it has near-complete coverage (121 fill pixels of 11,112,222 at SRER 2021) and its spatial pattern tracks woody vs herbaceous cover, so it can be compared against the AOP imagery by eye. Int16 with scale 0.0001 and fill 32767 - masked to NaN and scaled before writing, per instructions5.md 5.3 trap 1.
stage1_3_planet_grid.verification_window_note: Edge length of the two per-tile windows the cell grids are drawn in. A full-site 3 m grid is 11.1 million polygons and a full-site 1 m grid is 100 million; QGIS opens neither usefully. 60 m gives 20 x 20 Planet cells per window, enough to read a congruence offset by eye.

measured.note: MEASURED from US-xSR_NEON_Santa_Rita_Experimental_Range_PLSP_2021.nc by run_stage1_3_define_planet_grid.py, not assumed. The PlanetScope LSP pixel is 3 m, so N = 3 - earlier drafts of instructions5.md said 'expected 4' and that was wrong. Cached here for reference only; every script reads the live values from the netCDF via stage1_data_and_features/qa/planet_grid_SRER_2022.json.

stage1_3_planet_grid.crop_note: NEON tiles are cropped to the PlanetScope footprint, which is the smaller SRER focus area (x 510555-520554, y 3525546-3535548). Ground truth outside it has no Planet pixel to aggregate into and cannot enter Steps 3-6, so carrying it forward would inflate ground-truth area against a Planet denominator that does not exist. 520000_3532000 is the only configured tile affected, at 55.4% inside.

stage4_1_aggregation.min_valid_pixels_note: A Planet block is kept only if 8 or 9 of its 9 one-meter pixels are valid - i.e. at most ONE masked pixel. Replaces the earlier 75% rule, which at N=3 quantised to 7 of 9 and let a block through with two of nine pixels missing, 22% of its area unobserved. Set as a count, not a percentage, because N=3 makes percentages misleading: the only meaningful cuts are 7, 8 or 9 of 9.
stage4_1_aggregation.aggregate_from_mosaic_note: No SRER tile is congruent with the Planet grid in both axes, so tile boundaries cut through Planet cells on all four edges of every tile. Blocking each tile in isolation emits partial blocks around every perimeter, which then fail the min_valid_pixels rule and silently delete the tile edges from the fraction product. Aggregate from a site-wide mosaic, or carry a one-cell halo per tile.
stage4_1_aggregation.min_pure_pixels_note: A block is a PURE END MEMBER when at least this many of its 9 one-metre pixels carry the same class - 8 or 9 of 9. Set as a count, not a percentage, for the same reason as min_valid_pixels_per_block: at N=3 the only achievable hard-count fractions are multiples of 1/9, so instructions5.md section 5 Step 4's '>= 90%' rule admits ONLY 9/9 blocks, because 8/9 = 0.889 < 0.90. Measured on run 4: that silently discarded 70,467 shrub blocks under RF-A_C (101,561 -> 172,028, a 69% increase) and 50,676 under RF-A_D. A threshold that reads as 90% but operates as 100% is exactly the trap the retention rule already fell into.

stage2_1_labeling_zones.cluster_min_pixel_fraction_note: Clusters holding less than this share of site pixels are excluded from the coverage gate. k-means at k=16 produces degenerate clusters - measured at SRER, cluster 2 is 1 pixel across the whole 10-tile site - and requiring coverage of those makes the gate unpassable. Shares are recomputed from the cluster maps on every run of 4_2d and the excluded clusters are named.
stage2_1_labeling_zones.min_polygon_area_note: Class-specific per instructions5.md 4.2. 0 bare / 1 grass non-binding (median 64 / 81 m2). 3 tree 4 m2, small mesquite. 2 shrub 2 m2, typical creosote crown 1-3 m2; a 9 m2 floor sat at the shrub median and both excluded and contaminated the class.
stage2_1_labeling_zones.cluster_presence_min_pixels_note: A cluster counts as PRESENT in a role only if some tile of that role holds at least this many of its pixels. k-means is fit site-wide, so a cluster can be confined to one tile and therefore absent from the other role entirely - measured at SRER, cluster 4 is 10,173 px on 517000_3531000 (train) and zero on all nine other tiles. The coverage gate previously required every above-floor cluster in BOTH roles, which no amount of labelling could satisfy for test. 1000 px = 0.1% of a tile, below which a cluster is a boundary scrap rather than a stratum worth a polygon.

stage2_2_shrub_candidates.note: CHM-derived shrub candidate proposals. Bounds come from H_GRASS_MAX / H_TREE_MIN in parameters; only area filtering is set here. Candidates are proposals, never labels - each must be accepted or rejected by hand. The full candidate set is provenance only; hand review works from the stratified review subset, sized to clear the 50-per-class-per-role gate with margin.
stage2_2_shrub_candidates.review_rule: A shrub candidate is an accepted label ONLY where reviewed = 1 and rejected != 1 on that feature. Rejected is not a label. UNMARKED IS NOT A LABEL - the default for an unreviewed candidate is reject, not accept. There is deliberately no config switch to change this: an earlier reviewed_tiles key let a whole tile be declared swept, which would have promoted 650 unmarked proposals to labels at SRER in one edit, tripling accepted shrub from 296 to 946. A CHM candidate is a machine proposal until a human marks it.

stage3_1_classification.note: Cap on pixels contributed by any one training polygon. Pixels inside a polygon are near-duplicates, so beyond a few dozen they add weight without information - and unevenly, since a 1386 m2 bare polygon would otherwise outvote a 5 m2 shrub one 277:1. Run 1 used no cap; run 2 uses 100. Sampling is random within the polygon, seeded by BASE_SEED + year.

run_notes.1: Baseline. No polygon subsampling, 5 tiles, partial shrub review. Frozen; not reproducible under current defaults without --max-pixels-per-polygon 0 (see run_reproducibility in the run 1 report).
run_notes.2: Adds polygon subsampling at 100 px/polygon. Label state identical to run 1 (train shrub 844 px), so this isolates the subsampling change with nothing else moving.
run_notes.3_smoke: FOUR CHANGES AT ONCE relative to run 2 - do not read run 2 -> run 3 as a clean comparison, and do not attribute any change to a single cause. (1) Polygon subsampling retained at 100 px/polygon. (2) Shrub candidate review advanced from 401 to a larger fraction of the 1500 candidates. (3) Tiles 5 -> 10: five added by CHM shrub-band quintile stratification, taking site coverage from quintiles {1,5} to {1,2,3,4,5} (instructions5.md 2A). Train now spans Q1/Q3/Q4, test Q2/Q4/Q5. (4) Shadow masks on the ORIGINAL five tiles changed: run_stage1_6_detect_shadows.py pools its luma threshold across tiles, so adding five shifted the site-wide 20th percentile and re-cut shadow everywhere. Also note the k-means labeling zones were refit across all ten tiles, renumbering clusters, and a 0.1% cluster size floor was introduced so degenerate clusters (2 at 1 pixel, 11 at 0.08%) no longer gate coverage.
run_notes.3: The finished run 3: same configuration as 3_smoke (10 quintile-stratified tiles, subsampling at 100 px/polygon) but executed once labelling passes the gate in run_stage2_4_check_hand_labeling_progress.py. Compare against 3_smoke, not against run 2.
run_notes.4: SIX CHANGES AT ONCE relative to run 3 - not a clean comparison, and run 3 is not a clean baseline either since three of the six are corrections to defects present in it. Full detail in results/stage3_results.md section 11. (1) Two part-flown tiles replaced: 511000_3532000 (train, 4.09% flown) -> 517000_3531000, and 520000_3532000 (test, 24.37% flown) -> 516000_3528000. Every tile is now ~100% flown AND wholly inside the PlanetScope footprint, for the first time. In run 3 the 4.09% tile counted as a full training tile, so one leave-one-tile-out fold was a 4 ha fold. (2) Unflown RGB ground masked to NaN. NEON RGB declares no nodata and writes unflown ground as all-zero; helpers.read_rgb_at_scale now masks it. Affects 517000_3531000 only, 1.137% of the tile. (3) Shadow masks re-cut on every tile - the pooled luma threshold is site-wide, now 111.518. Shadow->tree roughly doubled on several tiles. (4) k-means refit, clusters renumbered. Run 3's cluster 4 was 100% unflown RGB and no longer exists; clusters below the 0.1% floor are now 6 and 7. (5) Label set changed BOTH WAYS: drawn polygons 423 -> 449, but accepted shrub candidates 350 -> 242, because the retired tiles carried 159 reviewed candidates and the new tiles carry 50. EXPECT SHRUB TRAINING PIXELS TO FALL from run 3's 2,087 - this is the one change likely to push a score down. (6) Gate logic corrected to require a cluster only in roles where it is present; no effect on training data.
run_notes.5: ONE CHANGE ONLY - the first clean single-variable comparison since run 2. Tiles, shadow masks, k-means clusters, features and code are all identical to run 4; only the shrub candidate review advanced. Reviewed candidates 569 -> 850 of 1500 (37.9% -> 56.7%), accepted 242 -> 296, shrub polygons 285 -> 339 (train 150 -> 183, test 135 -> 156). 517000_3531000 went from 0 reviewed to 77 and now contributes 28 shrub polygons instead of 2. THE QUESTION THIS RUN ANSWERS: run 4's shrub F1 fell to 0.636 from run 3's 0.676, and the run 4 note attributed that to shrub training pixels halving (2,087 -> 1,075) when the two retired tiles took their reviewed candidates with them. If that attribution was right, shrub F1 should recover here. If it does not move, the cause was the tile swap itself and not the label count. Also note the review rule was tightened before this run: the 'swept tile' shortcut was removed, so a candidate is a label only where reviewed = 1 and rejected != 1. Unmarked is never accepted. That is a code change but NOT a behaviour change for training - run_stage3_1 always applied the strict rule, so runs 1-4 are unaffected and remain comparable.
run_notes.6: ONE CHANGE ONLY - hand-drawn shrub polygons added to 515000_3526000. Tiles, shadow masks, k-means clusters, features, subsampling and code identical to run 5; no other tile is touched and no other class gains labels. WHY THIS TILE: it carries 7 shrub labels (0 hand-drawn, 7 accepted candidates) against 20-52 on every other tile, while having the site's highest CHM tree band at 13.5%. Most tall woody vegetation, almost no shrub training data. Held out, the model gives its woody cover to tree - 31.7% predicted tree against 13.5% actual, a +18.2 pp over-prediction, and its fold is the worst on the site at 0.668. The CHM shrub-candidate accept rate there is 7%, the lowest on site, so the candidate accelerator cannot supply these labels and they must be drawn by hand. See results/stage3_results.md section 13. THE PREDICTION THIS RUN TESTS, recorded before it runs: (1) the 515000_3526000 fold rises from 0.668 toward the 0.80-0.89 band of the other folds; (2) shrub->tree falls from 0.140; (3) TREE AREA BIAS FALLS FROM +5.41% WITHOUT A SINGLE TREE LABEL BEING ADDED, because 70% of tree's over-prediction is shrub leaking into it. (3) is the falsifiable claim - if tree bias does not move, the section 13.1 diagnosis is wrong and tree needs its own investigation. Run 5 baseline, RF-A_C: macro 0.855, shrub F1 0.658, tree F1 0.902, shrub bias -1.99%, tree bias +5.41%, shrub->tree 0.140, shrub->grass 0.176, train px 3,361 / 4,752 / 1,255 / 1,959.
run_notes.7: More shrub polygons drawn on 515000_3526000 (22 -> 29). CAVEAT RECORDED BEFORE THE RUN: the polygons sitting on CHM >= 2 m were NOT reclassified, only added to. The tile still has 40.9% of its shrub pixels on tree-height canopy (was 45.7%), a drawn-shrub median CHM of 2.85 m (was 2.86 m), and a shrub-vs-tree Youden J of 0.165 (was 0.145). Every other tile has a drawn-shrub median between 1.32 and 2.04 m. results/stage3_results.md section 15 measured H_TREE_MIN = 2.0 m as empirically optimal, so these labels still contradict the class definition and run 7 is expected to reproduce run 6 rather than recover run 5. One grass polygon was also added (14 -> 15), so the isolation is again not exact. Run 5 remains the reference until the >= 2 m shrub polygons on this tile are reclassified to tree or redrawn onto sub-2 m canopy.
run_notes.8: ONE CHANGE: six shrub polygons on 515000_3526000 reclassified to tree. No geometry was drawn, moved or deleted - only class_code changed, 2 -> 3, on the six polygons whose MEDIAN CHM was at or above H_TREE_MIN = 2.0 m and which were therefore tree by the section 3 definition. Selection was by measurement, not by row index, and the write went through a staged file with a round-trip check. Tile label counts: bare 5 grass 15 shrub 29 -> 23 tree 13 -> 19, 63 polygons throughout. No other tile touched. WHY: results/stage3_results.md section 15 measured H_TREE_MIN = 2.0 m as empirically optimal site-wide, then found this tile alone had a drawn-shrub median of 2.85 m against a drawn-tree median of 2.94 m - no height separation at all, Youden J 0.165, while every other tile ran 0.30 to 0.93. Six polygons of 21 to 75 m2 carried 47% of the tile's shrub pixels and sat on 2.1 to 3.1 m canopy. Runs 6 and 7 both degraded because of them. AFTER RECLASSIFICATION: the tile's J is 0.717 and its drawn-shrub median 1.29 m, in line with the site; shrub pixels on CHM >= 2 m fell from 40.9% to 5.3%. Site-wide J rose from 0.487 to 0.675 with the optimal threshold still exactly 2.00 m. PREDICTION, recorded before the run: tree area bias falls from run 7's +10.53% and shrub->tree falls from 0.226, both back toward or past run 5's +5.41% and 0.140. If they do not, the section 13.1 claim that tree over-prediction is shrub leakage is wrong. Run 5 remains the comparison point for the label-quality question; run 7 is the immediately preceding state. NOTE also that 1 polygon on this tile carries no class_code and is silently ignored by every stage.

tiles_note: 10 tiles, 6 train / 4 test. The original 5 occupied only site-wide CHM shrub-band quintiles 1 and 5 (train at the floor 0.116-0.121, test at the ceiling 0.373-0.546, site median 0.181), so the middle of the site was unrepresented. The 5 added tiles were chosen one per quintile from all 70 flown tiles, excluding anything within 2 km of an existing labelled tile. TWO OF THOSE FIVE WERE REPLACED on 2026-08-18 once stage 4_1 measured flight coverage - see tiles_retired. Quintile edges over the 54 eligible tiles: 0.116 / 0.132 / 0.157 / 0.188 / 0.291 / 0.546. Train spans quintiles 1,3,4; test spans 2,4,5.
tiles_pending_labeling_note: Downloaded and in the tile set, but carrying no labels yet. Stage 1_5 through 1_7 and all of stage 2 must run for these before stage 3 is re-run. NOTE that stage 1_6 pools its luma threshold across all tiles, so adding these two shifts the site-wide 20th percentile and re-cuts shadow on every tile - the same confound recorded in stage3_1_classification.run_notes for run 3_smoke. Stage 2_1 also refits k-means across all tiles and renumbers clusters. Clear this list once labelling passes the gate in run_stage2_4_check_hand_labeling_progress.py.
